title: Persistence and Browser Storage knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Persistence and Browser Storage”?
options: Persistence and Browser Storage means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Persistence and Browser Storage removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Persistence and Browser Storage should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Persistence and Browser Storage helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Persistence and Browser Storage helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Persistence and Browser Storage is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Local storage” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Local storage” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Local storage” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Local storage” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Local storage” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Local storage” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Local storage” under Persistence and Browser Storage. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Persistence and Browser Storage”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
